# iliad-021 — new renderings (Iliad 4.1–84)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| οἳ δὲ θεοὶ πὰρ Ζηνὶ καθήμενοι ἠγορόωντο (4.1) | "Now the gods, seated beside Zeus, were in assembly" | "Now the gods sat beside Zeus in assembly" | "were holding a council", "were conferring", "were speaking in the agora"; ἀγοράομαι is "be in assembly" |
| νέκταρ ἐοινοχόει (4.3) | "nectar was pouring out as wine" | "poured out nectar as their wine" | "served nectar", "poured nectar" alone (loses οἰνοχοέω "pour wine"), "was cupbearer" |
| δειδέχατ’ ἀλλήλους (4.4) | "were pledging one another" | "pledged one another" | "greeted" (kept for the Odyssey’s δειδίσκετο without a cup), "toasted" (anachronistic); keeps the Odyssey’s "pledged" for the cup |
| κερτομίοις ἐπέεσσι (4.6) | "with taunting words" | "with taunting words" | "mocking words", "cutting words"; the table’s κερτομίοισι is "with taunting ones" / "with taunts" when the noun is understood, here the noun ἐπέεσσι stands |
| παραβλήδην ἀγορεύων (4.6) | "speaking sidelong" | "speaking … in a sidelong way" (+ note: sense uncertain) | "insinuating", "by hinting", "with a sneer" (each decides the open question); from παραβάλλω "throw beside" |
| ἀρηγόνες (4.7) | "helpers" | "helpers" | "defenders", "protectors"; ἀρήγω is "help" (iliad-006) |
| Ἀργείη Ἥρη (4.8) | "Argive Hera" | "Argive Hera" | "Hera of Argos", "Hera the Argive"; follows the table’s Ἀργείη Ἑλένη "Argive Helen" |
| Ἀλαλκομενηῒς Ἀθήνη (4.8) | "Alalcomenean Athena" | "Alalcomenean Athena" (+ note: named from the Boeotian town) | "Athena of Alalcomenae", "Athena who wards off"; no derivation from ἀλαλκεῖν is claimed |
| φιλομειδὴς Ἀφροδίτη (4.10) | "smile-loving Aphrodite" | "smile-loving Aphrodite" | follows the Odyssey table’s φιλομμειδής (8.362) unchanged; this edition prints one μ here and at 3.424 |
| κῆρας ἀμύνει (4.11) | "his death-fates wards off" | "keeps his fates of death away" | "keeps death from him", "wards off doom"; κήρ "death-fate" (the Odyssey’s "the fates", 18.512), kept apart from κῆρ "heart" |
| τῷ δ’ αὖτε … αὐτοῦ (4.10–11, Paris unnamed) | "but beside him, in turn" | "but as for him" | naming "Paris" in `l` or `i` (the Greek does not); the note says who he is |
| ἤ ῥ’ αὖτις πόλεμόν τε κακὸν καὶ φύλοπιν αἰνὴν ὄρσομεν, ἦ φιλότητα μετ’ ἀμφοτέροισι βάλωμεν (4.15–16) | "whether again evil war and fearsome battle-din we shall rouse, or friendship among both sides we shall put" | "whether we shall stir up evil war and the fearsome din of battle once more, or put friendship between the two sides" | "dread battle-cry"; φύλοπις αἰνή "fearsome battle-din" and μετ’ ἀμφοτέροισι "among both sides" / "between the two sides" reuse the Odyssey’s version of the pair (odyssey-119, 475) |
| ἔσται τάδε ἔργα (4.14) | "how these deeds shall be" | "how these things are to turn out" | "how this matter will end" (decides the outcome) |
| ὣς ἔφαθ’, αἳ δ’ ἐπέμυξαν Ἀθηναίη τε καὶ Ἥρη (4.20) | "So he spoke, and they muttered, Athena and Hera;" | "So he spoke, and Athena and Hera muttered;" | "murmured assent" or "groaned" (each picks a force the verb may not have), "grumbled" |
| μεδέσθην (κακὰ δὲ Τρώεσσι μεδέσθην, 4.21) | "evils for the Trojans they were contriving" | "contriving evils for the Trojans" | "plotted" (kept apart from συμφράσσατο "devised" and φράζεαι "plan"), "were devising", "were minded to" |
| ἀκέων ἦν (4.22) | "was in silence" | "stayed silent" | "was quiet", "kept still"; ἀκέων is "in silence" in the Odyssey table |
| σκυζομένη (4.23) | "being sullen at" | "sullen toward" | "glowering", "scowling", "angry" (reserved for χόλος); σκύζομαι is "be sullen, sulk" |
| χόλος … ἄγριος ᾕρει (4.23) | "savage anger had hold of her" | "savage anger took hold of her" | "wild rage", "fierce wrath" (wrath is μῆνις); χόλος stays "anger" |
| ἅλιον πόνον ἠδ’ ἀτέλεστον (4.26; echoed by πόνον οὐκ ἀτέλεστον, 4.57) | "vain and unaccomplished" / "not unaccomplished" | "vain and unaccomplished" / "does not go unaccomplished" | "fruitless", "useless", "unfinished"; ἀτέλεστος keeps the Odyssey’s "unaccomplished"; πόνος "toil" |
| ἱδρῶ θ’ ὃν ἵδρωσα μόγῳ (4.27) | "the sweat which I sweated in labour" | "the sweat I sweated in my labour" | "toil and sweat", "sweat of my brow"; the noun and verb stay the same word in English |
| δαιμονίη (4.31) | "Strange woman" | "Strange woman" | unchanged from the table (iliad-006, 561): Zeus uses it to Hera again |
| ἀσπερχὲς μενεαίνεις (4.32) | "unceasingly you are eager" | "you are eager, without pause" | "relentlessly", "furiously"; follows the Odyssey’s ἀσπερχὲς μενέαινεν "unceasingly raged" / "without pause" and the Iliad row that keeps "unceasingly" for ἀσπερχές |
| ὠμὸν βεβρώθοις (4.35) | "were to eat raw" | "eat Priam and Priam’s sons and the other Trojans raw" | "devour", "swallow whole"; "devour" would hide ὠμόν; "raw" placed last so that it qualifies all the victims, as the Greek leaves it open |
| ἐξακέσαιο (χόλον, 4.36) | "you might heal your anger" | "you might cure your anger" | "appease", "assuage", "satisfy"; ἀκέομαι is "heal" |
| ἔρισμα (4.38) | "a great cause of strife" | "a great cause of strife" | "bone of contention", "quarrel" (νεῖκος, the previous word), "rivalry" |
| μή τι διατρίβειν (4.42) | "not at all to delay" | "do not hold up" | "obstruct", "wear down", "put off"; διατρίβω "wear away, delay" |
| ἑκὼν ἀέκοντί γε θυμῷ (4.43) | "willing, with a spirit unwilling" | "willingly, though with an unwilling spirit" | "with a heavy heart", "reluctantly"; θυμός stays "spirit" as in the Odyssey table |
| Ἴλιος ἱρή (4.46) | "sacred Ilium" | "sacred Ilium" | "holy Ilium" (reserved for ἠγάθεος); ἱρός is ἱερός, "sacred" |
| ἐϋμμελίω Πριάμοιο (4.47) | "Priam of the good ash-spear" | "Priam of the good ash-spear" | "Priam with the fine spear", "of the goodly lance"; follows the Odyssey’s ἐυμμελίην "of the good ash-spear" |
| δαιτὸς ἐΐσης (4.48) | "the equal feast" | "the equally shared feast" | follows iliad-005 and iliad-006 unchanged |
| λοιβῆς τε κνίσης τε (4.49) | "libation and savour" | "the libation and the savour" | "drink-offering", "smoke", "the smell of fat"; κνίση keeps the Iliad’s "savour" (1.317) |
| τὸ γὰρ λάχομεν γέρας ἡμεῖς (4.49) | "that is the prize we have received by lot, we ourselves" | "that is the prize of honour we gods have received" | "our due share", "our honour"; γέρας keeps "prize" / "prize of honour" |
| τρεῖς … πόληες (4.51) | "three cities" | "the three cities" | "towns"; πόλις stays "city" |
| εὐρυάγυια Μυκήνη (4.52) | "wide-streeted Mycenae" | "Mycenae of the wide streets" | follows the table’s εὐρυάγυια unchanged |
| τὰς διαπέρσαι (4.53) | "these sack" | "sack them" | "plunder" (reserved for ἐξαλαπάξαι), "destroy utterly"; διαπέρθω keeps "sack" |
| περὶ κῆρι (4.24 and 4.53, with ἀπέχθωνται) | "exceedingly at heart" / "beyond all … at heart" | "deeply … at heart" / "above them all at heart" | "dearly", "from my heart"; περί an adverb "exceedingly" at 4.53, a preposition "beyond" with τάων at 4.46 |
| τάων οὔ τοι ἐγὼ πρόσθ’ ἵσταμαι οὐδὲ μεγαίρω (4.54) | "In front of these I do not stand, nor do I grudge it." | "I will not stand in your way over them, nor do I grudge it." | "I shall not defend them", "stand against"; μεγαίρω keeps the Odyssey’s "grudge" |
| φθονέω … οὐκ ἀνύω φθονέουσ’ (4.55–56) | "I begrudge it" … "I accomplish nothing, begrudging" | "I begrudge it" … "I gain nothing by begrudging" | "envy", "resent"; φθονέω keeps the Odyssey’s "begrudge" |
| πρεσβυτάτην τέκετο Κρόνος ἀγκυλομήτης (4.59) | "me as eldest begot Cronus of crooked cunning" | "Cronus of crooked cunning begot me as the eldest" | "bore" (τίκτω of the father is "begot"), "first-born"; ἀγκυλομήτης keeps the table’s "of crooked cunning" |
| σὴ παράκοιτις κέκλημαι (4.60–61) | "your consort I am called" | "I am called your wife" | "bedfellow", "spouse"; follows the table’s παράκοιτις "consort" / "wife" |
| σὺ δὲ πᾶσι μετ’ ἀθανάτοισιν ἀνάσσεις (4.61) | "you among all the immortals are lord" | "you rule among all the immortals" | follows the table’s ἀνάσσεις "are lord" / "rule" |
| ὑποείξομεν ἀλλήλοισι (4.62) | "we will yield to each other" | "we will give way to each other" | "make concessions", "give in"; ὑπείκω "yield, give way" (the Odyssey’s ὑπόειξεν "gave way") |
| ἐπιτεῖλαι (4.64) | "give charge" | "give Athena the charge" | "order", "command"; follows the Odyssey’s ἐπιτειλαμένῳ "having given charge" and the Iliad’s "laid a strong charge" |
| φύλοπιν αἰνήν (4.65, 4.82) | "fearsome battle-din" | "the fearsome din of battle" | "dread", "grim"; as at 4.15 |
| ὑπερκύδαντας Ἀχαιούς (4.66, 4.71) | "the exulting Achaeans" | "the exulting Achaeans" (+ note: sense uncertain) | "overweening", "proud", "glorying" (each decides the open question) |
| ἄρξωσι πρότεροι ὑπὲρ ὅρκια δηλήσασθαι (4.67 = 4.72) | "might first begin to do harm … beyond the oaths" | "the first to start doing harm … in breach of the oaths" | "attack", "strike first", "break the truce" (decides how the harm is done); δηλέομαι keeps the Odyssey’s "do harm" |
| ὣς ἔφατ’, οὐδ’ ἀπίθησε πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε (4.68, whole line) | "So she spoke, and did not disobey, the father of men and of gods;" | "So she spoke, and the father of men and of gods did not disobey her;" | follows 2.166 ("did not disobey") with the epithet of 1.544 ("father of men and of gods"); "her" added in `i` only |
| αὐτίκ’ Ἀθηναίην ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα (4.69, whole line) | "At once to Athena winged words he spoke:" | "At once he spoke winged words to Athena:" | the table’s ἔπεα πτερόεντα προσηύδα unchanged |
| αἶψα μάλ’ ἐς στρατὸν ἐλθὲ (4.70) | "Very quickly to the army go" | "Go very quickly to the army" | "host" (kept for λαός / στρατός of a mass in the simile), "camp"; στρατός is "army" (iliad-011, 450) |
| ὣς εἰπὼν ὄτρυνε πάρος μεμαυῖαν Ἀθήνην (4.73) | "So having spoken, he urged on Athena, already eager," | "So he spoke, and urged on Athena, who was already eager;" | "stirred", "roused"; ὀτρύνω keeps "urge on", μεμαυῖα the Odyssey’s "eager" |
| οἷον δ’ ἀστέρα ἧκε Κρόνου πάϊς ἀγκυλομήτεω (4.75) | "Like a star which the son of Cronus of crooked cunning sent" | "Like a star that the son of Cronus of crooked cunning sent as a portent" | "shooting star", "meteor" (names more than the Greek); Κρόνου πάϊς ἀγκυλομήτεω is the table’s phrase (iliad-009, iliad-010) |
| τέρας … ναύτῃσι … στρατῷ εὐρέϊ λαῶν (4.76) | "a portent to sailors or to a wide army of people" | "a portent, either to sailors or to a wide army of people" | "omen" (kept for οἰωνός), "sign"; τέρας keeps "portent" (iliad-010, 324) |
| σπινθῆρες (4.77) | "sparks" | "sparks" | "embers", "flakes of fire" |
| τῷ ἐϊκυῖ’ ἤϊξεν ἐπὶ χθόνα Παλλὰς Ἀθήνη (4.78) | "Like that, she darted upon the earth, Pallas Athena," | "Like that star, Pallas Athena darted down to the earth," | "flew", "plunged"; ἀΐσσω keeps "dart" (ἀΐξασα "darting", 4.74) |
| κὰδ δ’ ἔθορ’ ἐς μέσσον (4.79) | "and she leapt down into the midst" | "and she leapt down into the midst" | "landed", "sprang"; "among them" (the Greek does not say of what) |
| ἦ ῥ’ αὖτις πόλεμός τε κακὸς καὶ φύλοπις αἰνὴ ἔσσεται, ἢ φιλότητα μετ’ ἀμφοτέροισι τίθησι Ζεύς (4.82–83) | "Truly either again evil war and fearsome battle-din will be, or friendship among both sides is being set by Zeus" | "Either evil war and the fearsome din of battle will come again, or Zeus is setting friendship between the two sides" | a question ("Will there be…?") — the edition prints no question mark; "peace" for φιλότης, which stays "friendship" |
| ταμίης πολέμοιο (4.84) | "the steward of war" | "the steward of war for men" | "master", "dispenser", "overseer"; follows the table’s ταμίης ἀνέμων "steward of the winds" |

## Departures from reused English

None. Every repeated line (4.25, 4.30, 4.39, 4.50, 4.79b–80, 4.81) takes the English the packet shows, unchanged; 4.66–67 and 4.71–72 are the same Greek in two places and carry the same English. No Odyssey wording has been departed from.
